title: Joel: old men shall dream (Joel 3:1)
hookLine: the spirit poured on all: "your old men shall dream dreams"

cards: Who gets to dream? The book of Joel opens with a disaster. Locusts, wave after wave, stripping the vines and the fig trees bare, until the fields mourn and the offerings stop.
Joel calls for fasting, for gathering, for turning back. Rend your heart, he says, and not your garments. And then, after the ruin and the return, a promise comes that has nothing to do with crops.
It's about who gets to see the future.

teach.b: In the King James words: "I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions."
All flesh, and then the text names who that includes.
Sons and daughters. The old and the young. And in the next verse, the servants and the handmaids, the people at the bottom of the household.
In Jewish Bibles this opens chapter three; in the King James it ends chapter two. Same words. Now notice the old men.
They aren't told to remember, or to advise, or to step aside for the young.

teach.h: YOUR OLD MEN SHALL DREAM DREAMS.
teach.b: They dream. Here, dreaming isn't the property of the young with their whole lives ahead. The spirit comes to the old, and gives them something new to see.
In the Torah, Moses hears that two men are prophesying in the camp, away from the tent where the elders gathered, and Joshua asks him to stop them.

teach.h: WOULD GOD THAT ALL WERE PROPHETS.
teach.b: His answer, in the King James words: "would God that all the LORD's people were prophets." Joel's promise reads like that wish coming true.

Not one prophet on a mountain, but a whole people, any age, any rank, the spirit poured out like rain on a field the locusts left bare. Joel doesn't say what the old men will dream. Only that they will.

how: Joel is one of the Twelve in the Hebrew Bible; Jews read Joel 2 as part of the haftarah on Shabbat Shuvah in some communities, alongside Hosea 14.

o: the prophet who promised the spirit poured out on all flesh
the prophet who said only the elders would see visions
a herdsman from Tekoa who was sent to Bethel

games.q: old men dream dreams — tap the pairs.
p: strip the vines and fig trees
wished all the people were prophets

s: in Joel, dreaming is promised to the young
the young men see visions; it's the old men who dream dreams.
Joel names servants and handmaids among those who receive the spirit
the promise goes out of its way to include them.
the verse is numbered the same in every Bible
Jewish Bibles put it at Joel 3:1; the King James at 2:28.

games.q: two men are prophesying in the camp, away from the tent. someone asks Moses to stop them. what does he say?
o: would God that all the LORD's people were prophets.
games.why: Moses wishes the spirit on everyone, and Joel's promise reads like that wish coming true.

practice: Whatever your age, there may be a voice somewhere that says it's too late, or too early, or not for someone like you; set it down for a while and let one dream come, a skill, a trip, a kindness, a thing you'd like to build or mend.
Don't plan it, just let yourself see it, the way Joel promises the old will dream. If you pray, you can hold it before God.

wordCard.voice: Joel. The prophet of the locusts, who promises a spirit poured out on all flesh, so that even the old dream dreams. Today's word.
